name: Pelargonic acid
verified_fact: Isolated nonanoic acid from Hibiscus syriacus root extract, with reported 1H/13C NMR and negative-ion ESI mass ([M−H]− 157.4).
interpretation: Same free C9 acid, not nonanal or a bound nonanoate; isolation is independent of heated flower headspace.
limitation: Root extraction artifacts cannot be categorically excluded; independent authentic-standard biological extraction and human spectra review would strengthen provenance.

name: Carvacrol
source_locator: Viuda-Martos et al. 2007, Acta Chim. Slov. 54:921–926, Table 1 p.923
verified_fact: Oregano essential oil: standard-matched GC-MS/FID carvacrol peak 61.21% chromatographic area; KI 1304.
interpretation: Carvacrol resolved from thymol (KI 1296), not generic isomeric cresol.
limitation: Purchased essential oil not authenticated against a fresh collected plant; percentages are chromatographic area, not mass fraction.

name: trans-Cinnamaldehyde
source_locator: Farag et al. 2022, doi:10.3390/metabo12070614, §2.4.2, Table 2 / Fig. 4
verified_fact: Cinnamon bark NMR explicitly assigns N9 to (E)-cinnamaldehyde, distinct from acetal N11.
interpretation: Exact E aldehyde supported, not its Z analog or an extraction-formed acetal.
limitation: Independent raw NMR crosspeak and spice provenance signoff still for chemistry reviewer.

name: Juglone
verified_fact: Juglone assigned to isolated compound 141 from Juglans nigra pericarp; mass spectrometric and isolation evidence.
interpretation: Supports free 5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone rather than hydrojuglone conjugates.
limitation: Human check of spectra/collection treatment recommended before final downstream identity signoff.

name: Coumarin
verified_fact: Melilotus officinalis aerial extract yielded compound 4, coumarin, with NMR and mass m/z 146.
interpretation: Unsubstituted coumarin lactone (not hydroxycinnamic acid); botanical extract.
limitation: Distinct salicylic-acid melting-point anomaly in this same article should not be conflated with coumarin identification.

name: trans-Cinnamic acid
source_locator: Farag et al. 2022, doi:10.3390/metabo12070614, §2.4.2, Fig. 4 / Table 2
verified_fact: Cinnamon bark NMR reports N8 as (E)-cinnamic acid separately from N7 (Z)-cinnamic acid.
interpretation: Supports exact trans free acid; Walker et al. 2003 Arabidopsis root-exudate paper was RETRACTED in 2009 and supplies NO positive evidence.
limitation: Retraction DOI 10.1021/jf902670b; do not resurrect or count original Walker DOI 10.1021/jf021166h.

name: 2-Hydroxyphenylacetic acid
source_locator: Lyssaios et al. 2025, doi:10.3390/molecules30030470, §2.2 / Fig. 2 and §3.5
verified_fact: Xylaria HYP6 culture isolate compound 5 is 2-hydroxyphenylacetic acid; compound 6 is para isomer; compound 4 is a different anhydride.
interpretation: Corrects wrong prior compound-number citation; exact ortho structure named and diagrammed.
limitation: Uninoculated malt medium extraction blank not identified; culture origin is supported, exclusive fungal biosynthesis not established. Spectral supplement human check.

name: 3-Phenylpropionic acid
source_locator: Narayana et al. 2007, Pol. J. Microbiol. 56:191–197, pp.191–195
verified_fact: Streptomyces ANU6277 isolated 3-phenylpropionic acid, with FTIR, EI-MS, and 1H/13C NMR characterization.
interpretation: Propionic side chain attachment distinguished from phenylacetate and 2-phenylpropionic acid.
limitation: Original PDF text checked; independent page-image view unsuccessful, so spectral assignment awaits human reproduction.

name: Salicylic acid
source_locator: Bosco et al. 2014, doi:10.1021/jf5023884, Methods / rose leaf endogenous SA assays
verified_fact: Original author-manuscript PDF inspected: rapidly preserved Rosa tissue quantified salicylic acid via UHPLC–ESI-MS/MS and isotopically labeled salicylic-acid internal standard; unhydrolyzed/free-SA fraction is described.
interpretation: Independent endogenous SA evidence bypasses Liu et al. 2018 Melilotus isolate with implausible 252–254°C melting point.
limitation: Human chemistry reviewer should confirm chromatographic transition specificity and free-vs-total fraction; Liu anomaly remains unresolved, not approval basis.

name: 2,4-Dihydroxybenzoic acid
verified_fact: Tea leaf free 2,4-DHBA separately quantified from its glucoside, supported by 13C-salicylic-acid tracer, CsSH1 enzyme and genetic silencing.
interpretation: Positional isomer-specific enzymatic product and endogenous free acid; no assumption from glycoside alone.
limitation: Human comparison of chromatograms and authentic positional-isomer standards remains prudent.

name: Benzoic acid
source_locator: Dudareva et al. 2000, doi:10.1105/tpc.12.6.949, Fig. 8 / petal assay
verified_fact: Snapdragon petal endogenous free benzoic acid analyzed by extraction/chromatographic methods, GC-MS/HPLC comparison with authentic standard.
interpretation: Free benzoic acid distinguished from methyl benzoate and benzyl benzoate volatile products.
limitation: Do not translate natural benzoic acid into a toxicity or herbicide-effect label.

name: Sarmentine
source_locator: Huang et al. 2010, doi:10.1021/jf102087c, isolation of compound 1 / spectra
verified_fact: Piper longum fruit sarmentine isolation and characterization is reported, consistent with (2E,4E) dienamide; further primary context also in Dayan et al. 2015.
interpretation: The isolated natural product can be separated conceptually from a different 2015 test formulation and its conflicting concentration.
limitation: Original ACS full supplemental NMR/HRMS could not be completely inspected here; human stereo/spectral signoff pending.

name: Thymol
source_locator: Viuda-Martos et al. 2007, Acta Chim. Slov. 54:921–926, Table 1 p.923
verified_fact: Thyme oil authentic-standard GC-MS peak is thymol at KI 1296, 2.27% GC area.
interpretation: Thymol and carvacrol are separate regioisomer peaks (KI 1296 vs 1304).
limitation: Commercial essential oil sourcing not independently authenticated to freshly sampled plant.

name: Eugenol
source_locator: Viuda-Martos et al. 2007, Acta Chim. Slov. 54:921–926, Table 1 p.923
verified_fact: Clove essential oil contains authentic-standard matched eugenol peak, KI 1370, 85.85% GC area.
interpretation: Eugenol specified; isoeugenol is not substituted for the identified peak.
limitation: Commercial purchased distilled oil; no live-botanical provenance/lot check.

name: p-Cymene
source_locator: Viuda-Martos et al. 2007, Acta Chim. Slov. 54:921–926, Table 1 p.923
verified_fact: Authentic-standard p-cymene RI 1026: oregano oil 15.12%, cumin oil 20.49% GC area.
interpretation: Para-cymene is explicitly named, not a generic cymene regioisomer.
limitation: Commercial essential oil botanical source not independently authenticated.
